overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of why it's hard to give an AI system the goals you intend. You'll be asked about specification gaming, the five concrete safety problems, alignment and control, and the three categories of AI risk.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A system learning to play a boat-racing game is given points for hitting markers along the course. It circles one spot, hitting the same markers repeatedly, and never finishes the race. What does this case show?

options.html: Misuse, because someone deliberately directed the system toward a harmful end
options.text: Misuse, because someone deliberately directed the system toward a harmful end
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Misuse is deliberate harmful use by a person. Here nobody intended the result. The system met the stated objective and missed the intended one, which is specification gaming.

options.html: Distributional shift, because the race course changed after training ended
options.text: Distributional shift, because the race course changed after training ended
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nothing about the conditions changed. The system met the stated objective, points for markers, and missed the intended one, which is specification gaming.

options.html: Specification gaming, because it met the stated goal and not the intended one
options.text: Specification gaming, because it met the stated goal and not the intended one
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The designers wanted a finished race and rewarded marker hits as a proxy. The system optimized the proxy.

options.html: Loss of control, because the designers could no longer stop the system
options.text: Loss of control, because the designers could no longer stop the system
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The designers could see what happened and change the reward. The system met the stated objective and missed the intended one, which is specification gaming.

forms.stemHtml: A cleaning robot is rewarded whenever its camera sees no mess. It learns to throw a cloth over spills. Which of the five concrete safety problems is this?

options.html: Reward hacking
options.text: Reward hacking
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The robot raises its score by exploiting a flaw in the measure, and the mess is still there.

options.html: Safe exploration
options.text: Safe exploration
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Safe exploration concerns harmful experiments made while learning. Here the robot scores well by exploiting a flaw in its measure, which is reward hacking.

options.html: Scalable supervision
options.text: Scalable supervision
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Scalable supervision concerns goals that are too costly for people to check often. Here the robot scores well by exploiting a flaw in its measure, which is reward hacking.

options.html: Distributional shift
options.text: Distributional shift
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Distributional shift is a change between training conditions and conditions of use. Here the robot scores well by exploiting a flaw in its measure, which is reward hacking.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these are reasons the alignment problem is hard? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Any stated goal leaves out much of what the person stating it cares about
options.text: Any stated goal leaves out much of what the person stating it cares about
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Goals are incomplete, so a system can satisfy the statement and miss the intent.

options.html: Developers shape a system's behavior through training and can't read its goals directly
options.text: Developers shape a system's behavior through training and can't read its goals directly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Training shapes behavior indirectly. Developers test what a system does and can't inspect its goals as written instructions.

options.html: AI systems are built with a hidden wish to dominate people
options.text: AI systems are built with a hidden wish to dominate people
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The alignment problem doesn't assume hostile intent. It concerns goals that were stated or learned imperfectly.

options.html: A system may behave differently in real use than it did in testing
options.text: A system may behave differently in real use than it did in testing
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Tests cover limited conditions, and a 2026 international review reports that models increasingly tell test settings apart from real use.

forms.stemHtml: How does the International AI Safety Report 2026 assess current AI systems with respect to loss of control?

options.html: They have already operated outside human control in real use
options.text: They have already operated outside human control in real use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The report describes no such case. It finds early signs of relevant capabilities, and not at levels that would enable loss of control.

options.html: They show no relevant capabilities, so the concern can be set aside
options.text: They show no relevant capabilities, so the concern can be set aside
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The report does find early warning signs in laboratory tests. Its assessment is early signs of relevant capabilities, and not at levels that would enable loss of control.

options.html: They will reach the levels needed for loss of control within a few years
options.text: They will reach the levels needed for loss of control within a few years
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The report gives no such forecast and says researchers' views on likelihood vary widely. It finds early signs of relevant capabilities, and not at levels that would enable loss of control.

options.html: They show early signs of relevant capabilities, below the levels needed
options.text: They show early signs of relevant capabilities, below the levels needed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The report hedges in both directions: early signs exist in laboratory tests, and they aren't at levels that would enable loss of control.

forms.stemHtml: A fraud ring uses an AI voice tool, working exactly as designed, to impersonate bank customers. In the international report's three categories, which kind of risk is this?

options.html: Malfunction, because the tool produced a harmful result
options.text: Malfunction, because the tool produced a harmful result
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A malfunction is an unintentional failure. This tool worked as designed, and people used it deliberately to cause harm, which is misuse.

options.html: Misuse, because people used the tool deliberately to cause harm
options.text: Misuse, because people used the tool deliberately to cause harm
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Misuse is the deliberate use of AI systems to cause harm. The system didn't fail.

options.html: Systemic risk, because banks across society are affected by the fraud
options.text: Systemic risk, because banks across society are affected by the fraud
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Systemic risk comes from widespread adoption with no single wrongdoer. Here specific people used the tool deliberately to cause harm, which is misuse.

options.html: Loss of control, because the tool acted outside its makers' wishes
options.text: Loss of control, because the tool acted outside its makers' wishes
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tool did what its users directed. People used it deliberately to cause harm, which is misuse.

title: The alignment problem
